content.thinking: ה Claude ha-kodem nir'a ascout ha-mapa shel hashkaot be-madad, ve-hem ha-sachli ha-ema-ahat ve-hazeher ahat ma-ha-sh-ha-sh-pi; ha-mchsu'ot ha-chadashot ya'alu sh'elot, ve-oni ha-chobeh she-achshav me'alim et ha-hasbarot l-gab'i ha-kaspim.

הטבלה השנייה מציגה תעודות סל, קרנות מחקות וקרנות צוברות, וצריכה לפחות בנקים המוכרים לי פסגות היא הזולה ביותר עם 86,492 ₪, בעוד שעמלת הפועלים מגיעה ל־6,576 ₪ לעומת 1,057 ₪ של פסגות. אני אסביר את המינוחים ואת המס על שינוי המטבע בהמשך.

content.text:
Now it's all English: "iShares", "Vanguard", "UCITS ETF". I can't read that.
Red bars on the right, more minuses, "−4,157", "−4,492".
"מזרחי טפחות 10,608"... my head is spinning. Too many numbers.
Who even made this? "מקור". Never heard of it. I'm stopping here.

**What I'd tell my son:**

"Darling, I looked at what Ruthie sent and I wouldn't decide anything with it. I'm quite sure. It opened with 'להשקיע במדד' and English letters, S&P, MSCI. To me מדד is the price index on the news. Then came sliders and a dark screen full of colourful little labels and minus signs everywhere. It isn't about deposits at all. It's dollars, shares and tax. And it's from a site called 'מקור' that I've never heard of.

I did see the first number, 86,492 ₪ against 'הפקדתם 70,000'. I saw that פסגות was marked 'הזול' and was at the top. My banks were below it, and next to them were numbers like 6,576 or 10,608 for '10 שנים'. If that's what the bank takes from me, it worries me. I'd like you to explain it to me or come with me to the bank.

I looked at four screens: the top part with the boxes and sliders, then a list of funds with codes on the left and banks on the right, then more English names and red bars. That's where I stopped. Didn't read the rest.

Words I didn't understand: מדד the way they use it, תעודת סל, קרן מחקה, צוברת, מחלקת דיבידנד, נאמן, DCA, ETF, UCITS, 'לא בחישוב', 'מס גם על שינוי המטבע', '(4D)'. Some of the lines under the boxes were small and grey, like the line with the dollar rate, and I couldn't read them properly.

What bothered me most: all the minuses (−43, −447, −3,671, −4,492) and the red bars. I don't know whether that's a loss or something else. There's too much going on at once. If it were up to me, I'd put one simple sentence at the top, like 'this is how much your bank takes, and this is how much you'd keep'. Without the English and without all the colours."
